newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Enterprise top job to first choice.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Enterprise top job to first choice.

text.p: Enterprise Oil, which earlier announced Pierre Jungels would become its new chief executive, said on Tuesday the British Gas' manager had been its first choice for the oil company's top job.
Meanwhile, Jungels, who has held his job at British Gas for less than a year, told Reuters that Enterprise Oil had made him an offer he could not refuse.

"It is a chance to influence a company directly and that is what I always wanted to do," said Jungels, who resigned as British Gas' managing director of exploration and production last week and will actually leave the job today.
Jungels will spend the coming months familiarising with Enterprise Oil before taking up his new position on January 1.
For some years, Enterprise has been looking to find a chief executive to replace Graham Hearne, who will continue as chairman, after having combined both positions since 1991.
To relieve Hearne, Enterprise in 1994 appointed Mike Pink as chief operating officer. Pink, 59, will retire at the start of the new year.
As it is company policy to have no executives older than 60, Pink was not considered to become chief executive, Enterprise said.
"Mike Pink has made an outstanding contribution to the operational success of Enterprise over the past two and a half years," Hearne said in a statement.
"Today's announcement is significant in that Pierre (Jungels) will have the responsibility of leading the group as chief executive into the next stage of growth," he added.

Enterprise, which failed to acquire rival LASMO in a bitter struggle in 1994, is currently expanding its operations from its traditional North Sea base into Norway, Italy, the Gulf of Mexico, South America and the Middle East.
Jungels, who joined British Gas in December 1995, said talks with Enterprise on becoming the firm's chief executive started two months ago.
"It is a successful company and now it is just a matter of familiarising and -- in discussion with the board -- finding out which way it is going to go in the next century," Jungels said.
British Gas has already started to look for a replacement both internally and externally.
David Varney, the chief executive designate of TransCo International, will combine Jungels' job with his current position in the meantime, British Gas said.
"He (Jungels) has had an offer he just cannot refuse," a British Gas spokeswoman said.
"To captain his own ship is a marvellous opportunity and we all recognise the attractions of that for him and wish him well," she added.
